event: Fuel cell VXE 600 could not get through the GCS Launch Wizard on the ground in the UK because of repeated failed critical system commands, delayed pitot test response and calibration failures; no flight occurred.
component: GCS (suspected; ground network or GCS processing, including mission simulation blocking uplink)
failure_mode: uplink outages from the ground side cause system commands to time out and be reported as failed
contributing: vehicle on older 6.1.2 firmware than released 6.3.4
high data rates (4 to 15 Mb/s) on the Diag2 payload port
GCS does not retry or health check before sending system commands

evidence.quote: Conclusion: At this point I suspect something on the ground network. Maybe a faulty GCS or Ethernet cables.
GCS Mission Simulation blocks the GCS from sending any messages to the vehicle which can create a vehicle connection timeout after 50 seconds.
After testing multiple days, I cannot recreate the issue without manually disconnecting link during the surface check part of the launch wizard.
The data averages 4-5 Mbs, but frequently spikes up to nearly 15mbs. New leading theory is that network data congestion is to blame.
Several odd errors/messages in logs indicating GCS socket errors, packet timeouts, and IMU error checks failed.

team_root_cause: Recorded link outage correlates with system command failures. Testing failed to produce conclusive evidence of exact cause. Suspect GCS processing or system link connectivity issues. Testing indicated vehicle is functioning correctly.

would_settle_it.what: GCS event and debug logs around each failed system command: whether mission simulation was running, socket errors and uplink gaps, and whether radio and Ethernet links were both active
Jason Scherer's final report with the link outage correlation plots

would_settle_it.file: GCS laptop and Ethernet cables used on 28 Aug 2024
would_settle_it.what: bench test of the customer GCS and cables, since the vehicle itself tested normal

attachments_read: 25844_RMA MOD KIT Quote for AC Qty 8 Fuse Expanded Payload  LM TIQ UK 250108-1 January 15, 2025.pdf.md
reasoning: Engineering could reproduce the failed servo and disarm system commands only by interrupting the link, and could reproduce a vehicle link timeout with GCS mission simulation alone. The failures happened on both radio and wired links and the vehicle tested normal in house, so the cause points to the ground side (GCS or its network) but no single part or mechanism was confirmed.
notes: RMA-459 holds only quotes and later RMA notes (MCM not responding, AV box replaced for WDT in 2025), not teardown findings for this event. FS2-2332 (GCS mission simulation blocks uplink) is relevant background; it was read for VXEP-608.

event: During UK T&E on 27 Aug 2024, the Land at ELZ setting on VXE 600's primary GCS was found disabled before landing after the operator disconnected and reconnected GCSs following mission upload; near miss, no damage.
component: GCS Launch Wizard landing zone selection
failure_mode: opening the Launch Wizard automatically disables Land at ELZ and selects Land at PLZ (undocumented designed behavior)
contributing: behavior not documented in the manual
operator swapped between two GCSs after mission upload
customer uses glide (ELZ) landings as the primary method

evidence.quote: Any time the launch wizard is opened it will disable the ‘Land at ELZ’ behavior and select ‘Land at PLZ’.
the operator disconnected the 1st GCS from the plane, connected a 2nd GCS, saved the mission from the plane onto the 2nd GCS, then disconnected and re-connected with the 1st GCS.
It seems like this is a safety feature that was built in to reactivate PLZ as the aircraft will most likely become non mission capable after an ELZ landing.
I agree that this behavior is probably desired generally and instead of changing anything in the software logic we think just documenting it in the manual would be adequate

team_view_in_comments: The system is behaving as designed.

would_settle_it.what: GCS event log to confirm the Launch Wizard was reopened (or the GCS reconnected) at the moment Land at ELZ changed to PLZ

reasoning: Software engineering stated that opening the Launch Wizard always resets the landing behavior from ELZ to PLZ, and the operator's GCS swap and reconnect sequence fits that. The reset is intended behavior, so the failure started in an undocumented GCS design behavior; the fix was a manual note.
notes: Root Cause field says only 'Behaves as expected'; the mechanism comes from Ted Trowbridge's comment. The AAR was not analyzed in the ticket to prove the wizard was reopened, hence medium confidence.

event: VXE 572 at the 29 Palms training event had multiple uncommanded VTOL launch aborts (climb abort and RTL) with no crash.
component: VTOL AP firmware 1.44 magnetometer and LRF fault handling
failure_mode: outdated VTOL AP sensor checks flagged magnetometer and laser range finder faults and triggered climb aborts
contributing: mismatched firmware across XCOMM 4.60, VTOL AP 1.44 and FW AP 6.05m with GCS 6.1.2
ADs for 6.2.9 and 6.3.4 not applied
center wing reports number 1, same as VXE 688

evidence.quote: DebugMsg Climb abort, VTOL controller fault
The Launch abort itself was reported as LRF and Mag faults. There have been multiple updates to the drivers handling these sensors in more recent updates.
The VTOL aborts triggered in this code (v144 of VTOL) would have passed in the newer releases.
Issue addressed in firmware updates (6.2.9 & 6.3.4)
Bad Mag fault detection and rejection.

team_root_cause: Operator Error: Firmware was not up to date or consistent across XCOMM, VTOL AP and FW AP. Errors that resulted in launch aborts would not have caused an abort in the latest software.

would_settle_it.what: VTOL magnetometer ratio test margin and LRF readings at each abort, to show the sensors were healthy and only the old thresholds tripped

reasoning: The VTOL log names the abort trigger as a VTOL controller fault from magnetometer and laser range finder faults. Engineers state the VTOL 1.44 code would have passed these readings in newer releases, and the 6.3.4 AD lists bad mag fault detection fixes. The aborts were the old firmware acting on its sensor checks, so the cause is narrowed to outdated VTOL AP sensor fault handling rather than a failed sensor.
notes: Designed aborts: scored on the mag and LRF fault inputs as judged by outdated firmware. No per-abort data analysis is in the export; RMA-365 induction PDFs are image only. The 6.3.4 AD text was read as background.

event: USASOC VXE 336 climbed about 10 to 15 ft on VTOL launch and then aborted and landed without an operator command or warning; a second aircraft (337) at the same site showed similar aborts.
component: GCS uplink to FW AP (suspected GCS mission simulation blocking uplink messages)
failure_mode: FW AP received no GCS messages for about 5 seconds during launch, declared lost link and triggered the designed launch abort
contributing: customer downgraded software to 6.1.2 on their own
a later 336 abort was triggered by a VTOL gyro fault
337 aborts were a low climb rate abort and a link loss abort (337 later found with a missing lift rotor bearing on motor 4 in VXEP-900)

evidence.quote: [15:30:51.895 1004.895] ap dbg: vt lost link during lch, aborting
initial analysis shows that the fixed wing isn’t receiving GCS messages for up to 5 seconds during launch. This is what leads to the launch abort.
V336 has the confirmed link timeout launch abort.
Root cause believed to be GCS mission sim preventing uplink messages which trigger link timeouts resulting in log messages.
[15:04:01.533 1852.533] ap dbg: vt lost link during lch, aborting

team_view_in_comments: V336 has the confirmed link timeout launch abort.

would_settle_it.what: GCS event and debug log just before launch: whether a mission simulation or mission update ran when the FW AP link timed out, and FW AP serial traffic at that time
VTOL log for the later gyro fault abort to see whether gyro data stopped

reasoning: The 336 log shows the VTOL launch abort was triggered by lost link during launch, and analysis found the FW AP got no GCS messages for up to 5 seconds while close to the ground station. The linked FS2-2332 investigation later attributed these FW AP link faults to GCS mission simulation blocking uplink, which the team believed applied here, but that was never confirmed on this flight. The abort itself worked as designed on a degraded uplink.
notes: The only converted attachment, XCEVLOG.TXT, is from tail 337 (not 336); it is 341 KB and was read by searching for aborts, faults, link faults, resets and version lines rather than line by line. It shows a 337 low climb rate abort and a lost link abort. Closed as cannot reproduce after aircraft were reported working.

old spare center wing with serial number showing 1
launch aborts from magnetometer ratio test at old 0.25 margin (VXEP-896)

Not investigated due to outdated firmware
Downgraded from flight critical due to the unsupported configuration of the firmware on the aircraft.
partial abort behavior resulting in the fixed wing autopilot attempting to fly the ELZ mission while the VTOL autopilot

team_root_cause: - Operator Error: Did not follow ADs to maintain the vehicle.
disagreement: The team names operator error in not applying ADs, but the crash flight itself was never analyzed: the consolidated report says "Not investigated due to outdated firmware". event: LM/NAWCAD VXE 644 rolled right and dived into the ground about 2 hours 51 minutes into a fixed wing flight; aircraft destroyed.
component: FWAP IMU (TDK MPU-9250) pitch-rate gyro on 9DOF daughter card 1710p01a
failure_mode: pitch-rate gyro read -1000 deg/s (full scale) intermittently, then the whole IMU output froze, corrupting the FWAP attitude solution in a single-string autopilot
contributing: no range or jump detection on FWAP IMU data
about 10 out of spec workmanship issues found on the FWAP daughter card
single-string FWAP sensors
IMU worked normally on later bench tests

evidence.quote: Pitch rate is reported -1000 degree/sec, then back to normal levels, then back to -1000 degree/sec.
For TDK MPU-9250, gyro full scale range is +/- 1000
It looks like the entire IMU output was frozen at the end of the log, likely indicating a complete failure of the IMU.
So far it looks like the capacitive pickoff within the MEMS itself.
About 10 out of spec workmanship issues found after removing the can on the FWAP daughter card 1710p01a.
All properties were getting updated with values and servos were responding.

team_root_cause: Failure of y gyro reading. Currently unclear what caused the failure

would_settle_it.what: photos of the 9DOF daughter card under the can showing the workmanship defects and any damage near the MPU-9250
decap or vibration and thermal testing of the MEMS gyro to confirm the capacitive pickoff failure

attachments_read: 24718_RMA Repair Quote 240910-2 for AC VXE-644 Warranty NAWCAD 240910-2.pdf.md
reasoning: The FWAP flight data shows the pitch-rate gyro pinned at the MPU-9250 full scale value, then the whole IMU output frozen, while the VTOL attitude kept updating, which names the FWAP IMU as the failed part. Bench tests later showed the IMU working, and the EE team suspected the MEMS capacitive pickoff and found workmanship defects on the daughter card, but the physical failure mechanism was not confirmed. So the part is determined from the log, with the internal cause still open.
notes: Sister aircraft 643 had an MPU-9250 that read ID 0 and could not connect (described in the history document); not the main event. Closed to the Bermuda Triangle list as cannot reproduce. Same frozen FWAP IMU failure pattern as VXEP-637 (VXE 401).

event: MARSOC VXE 458 fuel cell flights showed fuel valve at 100% and life at 0%, shorter than expected endurance, and the GCS 6.3.4 asked for a fuel cell firmware update that then failed to load.
component: GCS 6.3.4 fuel cell firmware update check
failure_mode: GCS recommends a firmware update for a first generation D450 fuel cell for which no new firmware exists
contributing: endurance shortfall unexplained: only 645 g of 868 g fuel recorded as burned
possible fuel mass entry error or fuel burn calculation recall
fuel cell itself reviewed as healthy (450 W)

evidence.quote: this is a First Generation D450 Fuel Cell, I think that the GCS6.3.4 has been recommending fuel cell update by mistake.
All AARs provided on the ticket indicate the XCOMM version was 0x04000045 which satisfies the minimum version (0x04000027) required to update the FC firmware.
Initial review shows that the fuel cell is healthy, and capable of producing 450W.
What is interesting, is that the system only recorded a burn of 645g of fuel, and the initial fuel weight was 868g.

team_root_cause: Believed to be a firmware issue

would_settle_it.what: GCS fuel cell dialog and version check messages, fuel mass entries at start, and fuel cell valve and life channels
code review of how the GCS decides a D450 first generation fuel cell needs an update

reasoning: The fuel cell specialist found the fuel cell healthy and said GCS 6.3.4 recommends an update for a first generation D450 that has no new firmware, and the AARs show the XCOMM met the stated minimum version, so the false notification points to the GCS update check. This is an engineer's belief without a code review or reproduction, and the endurance shortfall and odd fuel valve and life readings were never explained.
notes: Two issues on one ticket: the false firmware notification (main) and the reduced endurance with fuel valve 100% and life 0% readings (not determined). Closed to the Bermuda Triangle list as cannot reproduce.
